title: 180FW Pilots Train to Survive
description: F-16 fighter pilots, assigned to the Ohio National Guard's 180th Fighter Wing, participate in survival training in Waterville, Ohio, Aug. 8, 2020. The training simulates what a pilot may experience if they eject over water or behind enemy lines. Training for diverse, real-world scenarios ensures Airmen are fully trained, qualified, prepared and ready to deploy worldwide at all times.

transcript.text: I am Master Sergeant Rob Rogers. I'm a SERE Specialist, and today
we are conducting combat survival training for the 180th Fighter Wing.
Today, we put the aircrew through combat survival training,
where we try to prepare them for the event that they get
shot down, or have to eject over enemy territory.
So today, we are trying to refresh the skills that
they would need in order to facilitate their own recovery
if they were to find themselves isolated behind enemy lines.
We also did water survival training, to prepare them in the event
that they should have to eject over water, how to deal with
getting loose from their parachute once they hit the water, so how to
either disconnect from being drug or how to untagle themselves,
should the parachute land on top of them, how to make sure that their
floatation devices are good and how to use those
and then also how to get familiar with their life raft, which is pretty much
their only piece of equipment that's really gonna help protect them from
the elements, should they have to eject. Survival and evasion training
is important, because it's one of those types of training that
you don't really need it, until you do. Knowing what to do, and having
that mindset of "it could be me that's shot down. I could be
the one that ends up on the ground, the person who's-
who had to 'punch out' in enemy territory," so to have that
mindset just makes a big difference.
